name: Buddha Maya Gardens
summary: A garden hotel on the edge of the Lumbini master plan area, a short walk from the Sacred Garden and the Maya Devi temple, run by the Kathmandu Guest House group since it opened in 1998. A comfortable, calm base for dawn visits to the temple.
body: Buddha Maya Gardens opened in September 1998 and has grown from a small hotel into one of Lumbini's best-known places to stay. It is managed by the Kathmandu Guest House group, one of the oldest names in Nepali hospitality. Rooms face landscaped lawns and trees, and the main temples are roughly five minutes away on foot, which matters when you want to be at the gate for the 6 am opening.

The restaurant serves Nepali, Indian, Chinese and continental dishes, and the staff can arrange bicycles, cars and guides for the monastic zone and the Kapilvastu sites. It is a sensible choice for families, older travellers and anyone who values quiet and an easy walk to the Sacred Garden over being in the bazaar.
why: About five minutes' walk from the Sacred Garden and Maya Devi temple
Quiet garden setting for rest between early and late visits
Long-established management with reliable service and tours

faqs.q: How far is Buddha Maya Gardens from the Maya Devi temple?
faqs.a: The hotel is on the edge of the Lumbini master plan area, roughly a five-minute walk from the Sacred Garden and the main temples. That makes it easy to reach the Maya Devi temple at opening time, around 6 am, and to return for a rest in the midday heat before visiting the monastic zone later.

Buddha Maya Gardens is managed by the Kathmandu Guest House group, which has run hotels in Nepal for decades. The Lumbini property opened on 27 September 1998. Bookings can be made through the hotel or through us as part of a Lumbini itinerary.

faqs.q: Can Buddha Maya Gardens arrange trips to Tilaurakot?
faqs.a: Yes. The hotel can arrange bicycles for the monastic zone and cars with drivers for longer trips to Tilaurakot, Kudan, Gotihawa, Niglihawa and Ramagrama. If you book with us, we arrange a private car and a guide who knows the history of the Kapilvastu sites.

name: Lumbini Hokke Hotel
summary: A long-running hotel inside the Lumbini master plan area, near the Cultural Zone at its northern end, first built to serve Japanese pilgrims and now Nepali-owned. Quiet, simple and close to the World Peace Pagoda and the crane fields.
body: The Lumbini Hokke Hotel stands within the Lumbini master plan area, close to the Cultural Zone with the museum and research institute, and within easy reach of the World Peace Pagoda and the sarus crane fields to the north. It was built to serve Japanese Buddhist pilgrims, and its design still shows that influence, though it has since passed to Nepali ownership.

It is a quiet place away from the bazaar, with a restaurant and gardens. Reports from guests in recent years have been mixed on upkeep, so we suggest it mainly for travellers who value the location inside the master plan, near the monasteries and the northern wetlands, over polish. Ask us for an up-to-date view before you book.
why: Located inside the master plan area, away from traffic
Close to the World Peace Pagoda and crane fields for dawn walks
Quiet atmosphere suited to pilgrims and meditators

faqs.q: Where is the Lumbini Hokke Hotel?
faqs.a: It is inside the Lumbini master plan area, near the Cultural Zone at the northern end, which holds the Lumbini Museum and research institute. The World Peace Pagoda and the crane fields are close by, while the Maya Devi temple is about 3 km south along the central canal, a short e-rickshaw or bicycle ride away.

faqs.q: Is the Lumbini Hokke Hotel Japanese?
faqs.a: The hotel was originally built to serve Japanese Buddhist pilgrims, and its design reflects that history. It is now under Nepali ownership. Guests should not expect a fully Japanese-run hotel today; check current facilities and menus before you travel.

faqs.q: Is the Lumbini Hokke Hotel good for birdwatching?
faqs.a: Its location near the northern end of the master plan area makes it convenient for early walks to the World Peace Pagoda and the wetlands where sarus cranes feed from November to March. You can be in the fields at first light without a long drive from the bazaar.

name: Hotel Srinagar
summary: A family-run hotel on the slope of Srinagar Danda above Tansen, at about 1,400 m, open for around five decades and known for views of Dhaulagiri and the Annapurna range from its terrace at sunrise and sunset.
body: Hotel Srinagar sits above Tansen on the crest of the Mahabharat range, about 4 km by the link road from the town centre. It has been run by the same family for around 50 years and is often described as the first three-star hotel in Nepal's western hills. Its greatest asset is the view: on clear mornings from October to February the terrace looks straight across to Dhaulagiri and the Annapurna range, with Tansen's rooftops below.

The hotel is a short walk from the pine forest of Srinagar Danda, which makes sunrise easy. The trade-off is distance from the old bazaar; you will need a taxi or a 30-minute walk downhill to reach Sitalpati and the workshops. Rooms are simple and comfortable, and meals are served in the hotel restaurant.
why: Terrace views of Dhaulagiri and the Annapurnas at sunrise
Short walk to the Srinagar Danda forest and viewpoint
Long-established, family-run hotel with a calm setting above town

faqs.q: Can you see the Himalaya from Hotel Srinagar?
faqs.a: Yes, on clear days. From the hotel terrace you can see Dhaulagiri and the Annapurna range to the north, best at sunrise and sunset from October to February. From April haze often hides the peaks, and from June to September the monsoon usually brings cloud.

faqs.q: How far is Hotel Srinagar from Tansen bazaar?
faqs.a: The hotel is about 4 km by road from the centre of Tansen, on the slope of Srinagar Danda. A taxi takes around 10–15 minutes. Walking down to Sitalpati square takes about 30 minutes on steep paths, and longer coming back uphill.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Srinagar a good base for Rani Mahal and Ridi?
faqs.a: Yes. Tansen is the usual base for day trips to Rani Mahal on the Kali Gandaki and to the temple town of Ridi, and the hotel can help arrange jeeps. If you book with us, we arrange a driver and guide for these trips and time them around the sunrise view.
